title: Foundational local complex-analytic geometry
abstract: Develops a common Lean foundation for several classical local theorems in several complex variables: complex-analytic Weierstrass preparation with full germ uniqueness, Noetherianity of holomorphic-germ rings, finite projection for hypersurface germs, the holomorphic constant-rank normal form, and the finite-family local analytic Nullstellensatz. The imported development also exposes the arbitrary-ideal Nullstellensatz and regular level-set, submersion, and immersion consequences.

informal.LocalComplexGeometry.localAnalyticNullst: If a finite family of functions analytic at the origin has common zero set locally contained in the zero set of another analytic function, then a positive power of the latter is locally an analytic linear combination of the family.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.holomorphicGerm_isN: For every finite complex dimension, including dimension zero, the local ring of holomorphic germs at the origin is Noetherian.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.hypersurface_finite: A nonzero hypersurface germ vanishing at the origin admits a linear coordinate change whose local quotient is finite free over the base germ ring, together with an explicit prepared equation and a proper, surjective finite-fiber projection of the local zero set.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.holomorphic_constan: An analytic map of locally constant complex rank is locally equivalent, through analytic source and target coordinates, to the standard rank projection.
informal.ClassicalComplexWPT.classicalComplexWeie: A complex-analytic germ of exact order in one distinguished variable factors uniquely into a nonvanishing analytic unit and a monic Weierstrass polynomial whose analytic coefficient germs vanish at the origin.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.analyticNullstellen: For every ideal of the local holomorphic-germ ring, the ideal of germs vanishing on its local zero set equals its radical.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.holomorphic_regular: Near a regular point, the level set of a holomorphic map admits an analytic parametrization with an analytic local inverse on the level set.
